title: Tanzanian Okra Stew
community: Enjoyed across coastal and mainland Tanzania
author: Mama Salima
desc: Tanzanian Bamia — okra cooked in a spiced tomato-onion sauce until tender. The distinctive slippery texture of okra thickens the sauce naturally — a vegetable that is simultaneously the ingredient and the thickening agent.
longDesc: Okra stew is loved throughout Tanzania and the Swahili coast — the mucilage that gives okra its characteristic slipperiness dissolves into the sauce during cooking, creating a naturally thickened stew that coats ugali magnificently. Those who love okra adore its texture; this recipe converts even those who are unsure.
ingredients: 400g fresh okra — washed, trimmed, sliced into 2cm pieces
steps: Do not wash okra after cutting — excess moisture increases sliminess.
Heat oil. Cook onions until golden.
Add garlic, ginger, and spices. Stir 1 minute.
Add tomatoes. Cook 5 minutes until thick.
Simmer covered 15—18 minutes until okra is completely tender.
The sauce will be naturally thickened by the okra mucilage.
chefTips: Pat okra completely dry before cooking — moisture increases the sliminess dramatically.
Do not stir excessively — more stirring increases mucilage release.
cookingScience: Okra mucilage is composed of polysaccharides (primarily pectin and glycoproteins). When heated, these dissolve into the cooking liquid, increasing viscosity. The degree of sliminess can be reduced by: initial high-heat cooking (which partially breaks down the glycoproteins), acid addition (lemon or tomato), or minimal stirring.
sustainabilityTips: Okra is one of the most heat and drought-tolerant vegetables — perfect for Tanzania's climate.
healthBenefits: Very high in fibre — particularly soluble fibre (pectin).
Good source of vitamin C and folate.
culturalNote: Okra stew is the dish that divides people — those who love it adore its texture and the way it coats ugali. Tanzanian cooks know that proper preparation produces a much less slimy result than careless cooking.
